derivedFrom.custodyDiscriminator: a row assigns CUSTODY only when it carries an authoritySource; plane-opener rows state which plane a file reaches into and carry none. Filtering on disposition alone conflates the two and yields 13 false plane conflicts.

targetRule: ADR 0040 §2.1 — edge lands at the repository root (the root manifest IS the Host-Edge package); cloud lands under the independent nested cloud/ package; shared under the inventory-owned shared/ package. The ai/ prefix is dropped in every case.
correction: sourceSha initially recorded a neo-agent-brain commit while sourceRepository names neomjs/neo - the rev-parse ran in the wrong clone. Corrected to the neomjs/neo dev SHA the inventory actually ran against, verified clean at that head.

The first emission carried 178 rows from an EXTENSION-shaped filter that silently dropped every file without a .mjs/.yml/.yaml suffix. That dropped 8 identities: 7 belonging to PR #9 (harmless) and ai/mcp/deploy/proxy/Caddyfile (a real miss), while leaving 11 PR #9 targets duplicated here. Re-derived with no extension filter and with ai/deploy/** excluded by scope: 168 rows. Caught by @neo-gpt-emmy.

The 168-row emission was an authority-bearing SEED set, not the receive. Its custody discriminator (authoritySource present) excluded 47 tracked plane-dispositioned files, 19 of which the import closure could not rescue - including ai/daemons/orchestrator/daemon.mjs and the fleet server. Re-derived as roots-union-closure: 616 files. Reported by @neo-gpt-emmy and @neo-gpt.

The 616-row receive left 206 tracked ai/** paths with no disposition at all, including six mcp-server.mjs entrypoints, the fleet server, and the orchestrator control plane. Reported by @neo-gpt-emmy as the fourth blocker and gated by @neo-gpt on whole-tree reconciliation. Now 819 received, 18 to PR #9, 2 stays-engine, 1 retire, 0 unclassified.

Ten paths were received that should not have been. @neo-gpt-emmy dispositioned the same 206 independently and caught them: nine ai/examples/harnessEndurance/** files are an Engine subject (they benchmark Neo worker topology and are consumed only by Engine e2e), and ai/data/memory-core/lazy-edges.jsonl is genuinely ambiguous. My membership rule follows directory; ADR 0040 §2.7 follows subject, and an Engine subject can sit in an ai/ directory.

Final partition ruled jointly by @neo-gpt and @neo-gpt-emmy at 806/18/14/2 with zero ambiguous. Two corrections against my 809/18/11/1/1: nightly-e2e is a four-file Engine unit so the runner, digest and README join the explicit-stay plist rather than the plist following them, and lazy-edges.jsonl is retire rather than ambiguous.

Five rows still named cloud/ targets after the files were moved to shared/ as plane-neutral members. The manifest is the deletion authority for #17791, so a row that names a path the tree does not have is worse than a wrong plane: it is an instruction to delete a source whose destination cannot be verified. Caught by checking every target against the tree rather than trusting the write.

Unresolved-edge disposition from @neo-gpt, applied as ownership rather than string rewrites: 13 scripts whose only blocker was Cloud config are Cloud and moved there with their npm entries; postReleaseSync and lint-tree-json import Engine buildScripts, so they stay Engine and left the Brain; the 13-line zero-import sanitizer five MCP entrypoints need is received as a plane-neutral shared member. Repointing the strings instead would have made every import resolve while leaving Host-Edge scripts depending on Cloud configuration.
scope: neo-agent-brain#13 receives the Agent OS source EXCEPT ai/deploy/**, which Brain PR #9 owns. PR #9 holds 18 movers; this manifest holds 616. The #17791 source-deletion predicate is the UNION of both sets (18 + 616 = 634), never this manifest alone and never PR #9 alone.
population: Census roots (custody rows AND plane-opener rows) union their transitive ai/** closure, tracked files only, minus ai/deploy/** which Brain PR #9 owns. Custody rows alone lost 19 tracked files including the orchestrator daemon and the fleet server; the closure alone cannot find files nothing imports, such as the five per-server config templates. Neither source is sufficient by itself.
planeRule: Census disposition wins. Otherwise SUBSYSTEM MEMBERSHIP - the nearest census-dispositioned ancestor directory - with cloud-safety as an override: a module whose transitive closure reaches chromadb, better-sqlite3, @google/generative-ai or @chroma-core/default-embed never lands on edge. Membership beats reachability-as-assignment by 3.2x on cross-plane edges (176 vs 562): "could this run on edge" and "whose subsystem is this" are different questions, and only the second predicts where the coupling is.
specifierRule: Every relative specifier is RECOMPUTED from the plane map, never preserved - a file moving from ai/x/ to cloud/x/ changes depth relative to a target that stayed at the root. src/** specifiers become the published Engine package (neo.mjs/src/**) per ADR 0040 section 2.3.

generatedConfigOverlays.cause: All six are gitignored and produced by ai/scripts/setup/initServerConfigs.mjs at npm prepare, which copies each tracked config.template.mjs over its gitignored sibling. The five per-server templates carry edge/cloud dispositions and travel; their generator carries retire. The Brain therefore receives the templates and no way to materialize them.
generatedConfigOverlays.owner: neomjs/neo#17787 — the per-server half needs the plane-owned bootstrap its own retire rationale already promises.

residual.tests: ZERO test files are received. ADR 0040 section 2.7 makes test custody follow SUBJECT, not directory, so the inventory row matching /ai/ by path is a census SEED to classify rather than a move set. An exact subject-owned test census is required before this receive is complete. Raised by @neo-gpt-emmy.

enginePackageStaleness.finding: neo.mjs@13.1.0 was published 2026-07-03, predates the cut, and still ships the entire Agent OS: 500 ai/ files in the tarball, 466 of them .mjs and resolvable from this repository as neo.mjs/ai/** right now. The Brain therefore depends on a package containing a stale copy of the Brain, and the failure is silent by construction because such an import resolves and the module loads.

liveOccurrence.note: Pre-existing example content, correct before the cut because that was genuinely how an external workspace reached the Agent OS. NOT rewritten here: its correct post-split form depends on an unanswered question — how does an external workspace reach the Agent OS once it is a separate, unpublished repository? Answering that inside a receive PR would be inventing the answer.

enginePackageStaleness.boundsResolutions: Two straddles blocking the workflow receive point at files that postdate the release, so reaching them through neo.mjs is unavailable even in principle: apps/agentos/config/cockpitSources.mjs (added 2026-08-08) and buildScripts/util/check-aiconfig-antipatterns.mjs (added 2026-07-16). Its sibling check-aiconfig-test-mutation.mjs (2026-06-14) IS in 13.1.0, so a Brain-side config lint would be half-enforceable.
enginePackageStaleness.notExposed: All ten neo.mjs/src/** specifiers this receive rewrote are present in 13.1.0, verified against the tarball rather than the tree. The receive itself is unaffected.
enginePackageStaleness.owner: neomjs/neo#17787 / neomjs/neo#17791 — a neo.mjs/ai/** specifier guard is the obvious mitigation with a clean sunset (it retires the moment an Engine release ships without ai/, which #17791 causes), but the same outcome arrives free with the next publish.

workflowReceive.finding: Brain has only substrate-sync.yml, so deleting config-template-ssot-lint.yml and identity-engine-coherence-lint.yml from the Engine drops enforcement with no receiver. Both lint scripts and every input are received; the workflows cannot be recreated because each has one genuine straddle.

straddles.note: a 29-line frozen constant in the Engine cockpit app; exactly one field is read (.roster)

read for ADR-0019 two-way ownership. This is the inverse straddle neomjs/neo#17783 named in its own problem statement: a stay-side guard whose subject departs goes green forever. Now concrete rather than forecast.

workflowReceive.reason: Recreating them now would produce two receivers that fail on their first run, which is worse than the gap they were meant to close.

brainCoupledOutsideAi.finding: This manifest partitions ai/**, so anything Brain-owned or Brain-coupled outside that prefix was structurally invisible to it however complete the partition looked. harness/** (received at 642d4ae) and the 82 npm entrypoints were both found this way, one report at a time. This is the enumeration so the rest are not.
brainCoupledOutsideAi.method: tracked files outside ai/, not already received, whose text references a path this receive actually took
brainCoupledOutsideAi.note: These are NOT all movers. Most are Engine files that legitimately reference Brain surface and need REPOINTING or severing, not relocation - the apps/agentos cockpit, buildScripts, the retained workflows. The per-harness agent hooks (.claude, .codex, .kimi-code) are a genuine open question: they are Agent OS configuration, but both repositories host agents, so duplication may be correct where it is wrong everywhere else.
brainCoupledOutsideAi.owner: neomjs/neo#17791 for severing, neomjs/neo#17787 for any custody call

wholeTreeReconciliation.note: A closure alone reached 616 of these. The gap was that root-script rows carry their executable inside evidence.command as a string while evidence.targets is empty, so a consumer keying on targets loses every npm-script entrypoint — six mcp-server.mjs among them — and losing an entrypoint loses its whole service tree. Recovering them from the command string added 86 files; a further 117 are unimported leaves no closure can reach and were classified by subsystem membership.
